metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the average number of queries received by DNS server in each second. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \DNS\Total Query Received/sec

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the average number of reponses sent by DNS server in each second. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \DNS\Total Response Sent/sec

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the number of LDAP successful binds per second for the NTDS object. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \DirectoryServices(NTDS)\LDAP Successful Binds/sec

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the ratio of Memory\Committed Bytes to the Memory\Commit Limit. Committed memory is the physical memory in use for which space has been reserved in the paging file should it need to be written to disk. The commit limit is determined by the size of the paging file. If the paging file is enlarged, the commit limit increases, and the ratio is reduced. This counter displays the current percentage value only; it is not an average. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Memory\% Committed Bytes In Use

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the percentage of elapsed time that the processor spends to execute a non-Idle thread. It is calculated by measuring the percentage of time that the processor spends executing the idle thread and then subtracting that value from 100%. (Each processor has an idle thread that consumes cycles when no other threads are ready to run). This counter is the primary indicator of processor activity, and displays the average percentage of busy time observed during the sample interval. It should be noted that the accounting calculation of whether the processor is idle is performed at an internal sampling interval of the system clock (10ms). On todays fast processors, % Processor Time can therefore underestimate the processor utilization as the processor may be spending a lot of time servicing threads between the system clock sampling interval. Workload based timer applications are one example  of applications  which are more likely to be measured inaccurately as timers are signaled just after the sample is taken. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the number of times that clients use a ticket to authenticate to this computer per second. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Security System-Wide Statistics\Kerberos Authentications

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the number of NTLM authentications processed per second for the Active Directory on this domain contrller or for local accounts on this member server. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Security System-Wide Statistics\NTLM Authentications

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the percentage of elapsed time that all of dns process threads used the processor to execute instructions. An instruction is the basic unit of execution in a computer, a thread is the object that executes instructions, and a process is the object created when a program is run. Code executed to handle some hardware interrupts and trap conditions are included in this count. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Process(dns)\% Processor Time

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the percentage of elapsed time that all of lsass process threads used the processor to execute instructions. An instruction is the basic unit of execution in a computer, a thread is the object that executes instructions, and a process is the object created when a program is run. Code executed to handle some hardware interrupts and trap conditions are included in this count. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \Process(lsass)\% Processor Time

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: This metric indicates the average number of searches per second for the NTDS object. It is backed by performance counter data from the domain controller, and can be filtered or splitted by role instance.
metricSpecifications.name: \DirectoryServices(NTDS)\LDAP Searches/sec

Resend domain verification ownership email containing steps on how to verify a domain for a given certificate order
This method is used to obtain the site seal information for an issued certificate. A site seal is a graphic that the certificate purchaser can embed on their web site to show their visitors information about their SSL certificate. If a web site visitor clicks on the site seal image, a pop-up page is displayed that contains detailed information about the SSL certificate. The site seal token is used to link the site seal graphic image to the appropriate certificate details pop-up page display when a user clicks on the site seal. The site seal images are expected to be static images and hosted by the reseller, to minimize delays for customer page load times.

operations.description:
A session is best for client device scenarios where developers want to authorize a client device to perform only a liveness detection without granting full access to their resource. Created sessions have a limited life span and only authorize clients to perform the desired action before access is expired.
Permissions includes...
* Ability to call /detectLiveness/singleModal for up to 3 reties.
* A token lifetime of 10 minutes.
Remarks:
Client access can be revoked by deleting the session using the Delete Liveness Session operation. To retrieve a result, use the Get Liveness Session. To audit the individual requests that a client has made to your resource, use the List Liveness Session Audit Entries.
operations.name: Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/Face/detectliveness/singlemodal/sessions/action

operations.description:
A session is best for client device scenarios where developers want to authorize a client device to perform only a liveness detection without granting full access to their resource. Created sessions have a limited life span and only authorize clients to perform the desired action before access is expired.
Permissions includes...
* Ability to call /detectLiveness/singleModal for up to 3 reties.

No action is needed in terms of the cache size. More than 100% means that the cluster's disk space is not large enough to accommodate the hot data, as defined by your caching policies. metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The amount of storage used by the storage account. For standard storage accounts, it's the sum of capacity used by blob, table, file, and queue. For premium storage accounts and Blob storage accounts, it is the same as BlobCapacity or FileCapacity.
metricSpecifications.name: UsedCapacity

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The number of requests made to a storage service or the specified API operation. This number includes successful and failed requests, as well as requests which produced errors. Use ResponseType dimension for the number of different type of response.
metricSpecifications.name: Transactions

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The amount of ingress data, in bytes. This number includes ingress from an external client into Azure Storage as well as ingress within Azure.
metricSpecifications.name: Ingress

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The amount of egress data. This number includes egress to external client from Azure Storage as well as egress within Azure. As a result, this number does not reflect billable egress.
metricSpecifications.name: Egress

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The average time used to process a successful request by Azure Storage. This value does not include the network latency specified in SuccessE2ELatency.
metricSpecifications.name: SuccessServerLatency

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The average end-to-end latency of successful requests made to a storage service or the specified API operation, in milliseconds. This value includes the required processing time within Azure Storage to read the request, send the response, and receive acknowledgment of the response.
metricSpecifications.name: SuccessE2ELatency

metricSpecifications.displayDescription: The percentage of availability for the storage service or the specified API operation. Availability is calculated by taking the TotalBillableRequests value and dividing it by the number of applicable requests, including those that produced unexpected errors. All unexpected errors result in reduced availability for the storage service or the specified API operation.
metricSpecifications.name: Availability

operations.description:
Delete a dataset.

Delete-time dependency validation is enforced. A dataset cannot be deleted while one or more jobs
still reference it as an input or output through `JobProperties.inputs` or `JobProperties.outputs`
(via `JobDataset.dataset`). If any consuming job exists, the delete is rejected with the
`ResourceDeleteHasActiveConsumers` error (code `ARB-RP-228`) and the dataset is not deleted. The error reports the total
number of consumers and returns links to the consuming jobs, each with the property path of the reference.

Required steps before deleting a dataset:
1. Identify every job whose `properties.inputs` or `properties.outputs` reference this dataset.
2. For each consuming job, either update it to remove the reference to this dataset or delete the job
(and, where applicable, the pipeline that contains it).
3. Once no job references this dataset, retry this delete request.

The delete is performed asynchronously: the service returns 202 Accepted with a Location header
to poll, or 204 No Content when the dataset does not exist.
operations.name: Microsoft.ResourceBuilder/workspaces/datasets/delete

operations.description:
Delete a workspace.

Deleting a workspace cascades to all child resources (datasets, data connections, pipelines, jobs,
and runs), which are removed as part of the ARM delete. A workspace is not subject to active-consumer
dependency validation, so this delete is not blocked by references between its child resources.

The cascade is performed asynchronously: the service returns 202 Accepted with a Location header
to poll, or 204 No Content when the workspace does not exist.

operations.description:
Delete a job.

Delete-time dependency validation is enforced. A job cannot be deleted while its parent pipeline
still references it by name through `PipelineProperties.activities[].job` (a `ReferencePipelineJob`).
If the parent pipeline references this job, the delete is rejected with the
`ResourceDeleteHasActiveConsumers` error (code `ARB-RP-228`) and the job is not deleted. The error reports the consuming
pipeline and the property path of the reference.

Required steps before deleting a job:
1. Update the parent pipeline to remove the activity that references this job, or delete the pipeline.
2. Once no pipeline activity references this job, retry this delete request.

The delete is performed asynchronously: the service returns 202 Accepted with a Location header
to poll, or 204 No Content when the job does not exist.

operations.description:
Delete a data connection.

Delete-time dependency validation is enforced. A data connection cannot be deleted while one or
more datasets in the same workspace still reference it through `DatasetProperties.connection.id`.
If any consuming dataset exists, the delete is rejected with the `ResourceDeleteHasActiveConsumers`
error (code `ARB-RP-228`) and the data connection is not deleted. The error reports the total number of consumers and
returns links to the consuming datasets, each with the property path of the reference.

Required steps before deleting a data connection:
1. Identify every dataset in the workspace whose `properties.connection.id` references this data connection.
2. For each consuming dataset, either update it to reference a different data connection (detach)
or delete the dataset.
3. Once no dataset references this data connection, retry this delete request.

The delete is performed asynchronously: the service returns 202 Accepted with a Location header
to poll, or 204 No Content when the data connection does not exist.

operations.description:
Update a Rule. The PATCH body is discriminated by `kind` and must match the existing rule's kind. For `eduQualification` rules, only `supplementalDocuments` is patchable, and only when `evaluationState == actionRequired`. For `businessVerification` rules, the patchable fields are `supplementalDocuments` and `externalId`, and only when `evaluationState` is `pending` or `actionRequired`. For `uboVerification` rules, the only patchable field is `attestation`, and only when `evaluationState` is `actionRequired` or `failed`; submitting a PATCH re-triggers provider evaluation of the UBO rule and resets downstream dependent rules. The UBO `users` list and `businessOwnership` are both server-provided (`users` from the configured provider, `businessOwnership` from the billing account sold-to) — neither is patchable. `payeeVerification`, `remQualification`, and `legalContactVerification` have no patchable fields today; PATCH on those kinds is rejected with 400 InvalidParameterValue. All other field/state combinations are rejected with 400 InvalidParameterValue or 409 RuleNotActionable.
Create or update a Rule. Rules are created by the service when the parent
assessment is created; they are not directly creatable by end users. Customer
PUT calls are rejected at runtime with `OperationNotAllowed`. Use PATCH to
modify rule fields that the customer is authorized to change.
operations.name: Microsoft.BillingTrust/assessments/rules/write

operations.description:
Get a Rule
List Rule resources by Assessment
operations.name: Microsoft.BillingTrust/assessments/rules/read

operations.description:
Appeal a rule's failed outcome by submitting a set of previously-uploaded
documents (typically one per reviewer-requested document type). Accepted
synchronously when the rule is `appealable` and the documents are valid; the
rule then scans the documents, forwards them to the verification provider, and
transitions to `underReview` asynchronously. Rejected when the rule is not
`appealable` or a document type is not among `documentTypeCodes`.
operations.name: Microsoft.BillingTrust/assessments/rules/appeal/action

operations.description: Start identity verification (IDV) for one or more of a `uboVerification` rule's individuals. Each directive targets an already-resolved UBO (by its `id` from `users[].id`) and drives that individual through the provider's identity-verification flow: `generateLink` returns a link; `sendSms` also sends the link to the individual via SMS. Returns the per-individual outcome (generated link, whether an SMS was sent, and the resulting state). Valid only for `uboVerification` rules while the rule is awaiting identity verification or has failed; it does NOT re-run business verification. Rejected with 400 InvalidParameterValue (wrong kind or invalid directive) or 409 RuleNotActionable (wrong state).
operations.name: Microsoft.BillingTrust/assessments/rules/startIndividualVerification/action
